title: channel_posts schema + migration (RLS + explicit-tenant-filter, indexes, 30-day expires_at, per-session keyed upsert)

story.i_want_to: add a tenant-scoped channel_posts table (RLS enabled, but queried via AdminRepo with an explicit tenant_id filter like all other tenant content) whose rows are project-scoped messages with an optional per-session upsert key and a uniform 30-day expires_at
story.so_that: agent sessions on the same repo (across machines) have a shared, short-lived, multi-machine coordination store to build the post/read API on

rationale: The coordination bus is the third memory plane (Knowledge=durable, Memory=agent-private, Channel=repo-scoped/transient). It must be hosted (multi-machine) and tenant-isolated by the same discipline as every other loopctl content table — AdminRepo (BYPASSRLS) plus explicit tenant_id filtering in every query, with RLS enabled as defense-in-depth. The schema is deliberately minimal — no message-type taxonomy — because the fleet audit showed the category taxonomy was essentially unused; an optional key gives per-session upsert for keyed working-state without a type system.

background.includes: Mirrors the tenant_id + AdminRepo pattern of Loopctl.Knowledge.Article and Loopctl.Projects.Project; RLS enabled via Loopctl.Repo.RlsHelpers.enable_rls/1 exactly as create_projects (20260327154649) and create_articles (20260410002347) do.

acceptance_criteria.description: A migration creates channel_posts with columns: id (binary_id pk), tenant_id (binary_id, references(:tenants, on_delete: :delete_all), not null), project_id (binary_id, references(:projects, on_delete: :delete_all), not null), agent_id (binary_id, not null), session_id (text, null), host (text, null), key (text, null), body (text, not null), refs (map/jsonb, null), expires_at (utc_datetime_usec, not null), inserted_at/updated_at timestamps.

RLS is ENABLED on channel_posts via RlsHelpers.enable_rls(:channel_posts) (defense-in-depth). NOTE: production isolation is NOT RLS — it is AdminRepo + an explicit tenant_id filter in every Coordination query (the Knowledge/Projects pattern). Both must hold: a query missing the tenant_id filter is a bug even though RLS would also stop it.

Indexes exist: a recency index for recent reads; an (expires_at) index for the sweep; and the PARTIAL UNIQUE index channel_posts_session_key_uidx WHERE key IS NOT NULL. AS SHIPPED the slot tuple is (tenant_id, project_id, agent_id, session_id, key) and the recency index is channel_posts_recent_seq_idx on (tenant_id, project_id, inserted_at DESC, seq DESC). History: the create migration (20260717020000_create_channel_posts.exs) declared the slot as (tenant_id, project_id, session_id, key) and a recency index channel_posts_recent_idx on (tenant_id, project_id, inserted_at DESC); 20260718000000_harden_channel_posts_slot_and_ordering.exs then DROPS and recreates channel_posts_session_key_uidx WITH the server-stamped agent_id in the tuple (so a spoofed, client-supplied session_id can never collide with — nor, via US-39.2's upsert, overwrite — another agent's slot) and adds seq (bigserial) plus channel_posts_recent_seq_idx; 20260718130000_drop_redundant_channel_posts_recent_idx.exs then DROPS channel_posts_recent_idx, a redundant prefix of the seq index. So the key slot is per (tenant, project, AGENT, SESSION) — NOT project-global and NOT session-only — and two concurrent sessions (or two agents) writing key "session_goal" do not clobber each other (see M7 for the per-session decision, US-39.2 AC-39.2.5 for the agent_id hardening and the partial-index conflict_target it forces).

Loopctl.Coordination.ChannelPost schema defines the fields, @derive Jason.Encoder exposing id/tenant_id/project_id/agent_id/session_id/host/key/body/refs/expires_at/inserted_at/updated_at, and a create_changeset that casts ONLY [:session_id, :host, :key, :body, :refs] — tenant_id, project_id, agent_id, expires_at are set programmatically on the struct, never via cast. There is NO :kind/:category/:type field.

create_changeset validates: body present and length <= 16384; key (when present) length <= 200; refs (when present) is a map whose keys are a subset of the allowlist {file, pr, branch, commit}, each value a string <= 512 chars, with a total serialized refs size <= 4KB (larger/other-keyed refs are invalid).

A secret denylist (the same regex set the knowledge extractor uses: Bearer/sk-/lc_/gh[pousr]_/AKIA/PEM/xox) is run over body AND every refs value AND key. A match REJECTS the write with a 422 (does not persist) so the caller learns the info did not land — it is NOT silently dropped.
The new table + indexes are online-safe (new table; no destructive rewrite) and the migration runs clean via the release migrate path.

test_cases.name: row inserts with programmatic tenant/project/agent/expires
steps: Insert a ChannelPost via Coordination with tenant_id/project_id/agent_id/expires_at set on the struct and body cast from attrs

test_cases.name: isolation holds on BOTH paths (AdminRepo+filter AND RLS)
preconditions: a post exists for tenant_a's project
steps: AND query channel_posts through the RLS Repo under tenant_b scope
expected_results: AdminRepo path: zero rows (explicit tenant filter)

test_cases.name: per-session keyed slot: two sessions do not clobber
preconditions: session A post key "session_goal"; session B post same key
steps: Insert both keyed posts with different session_id
expected_results: both rows persist (unique index includes session_id)

test_cases.name: over-large / wrong-keyed refs rejected
expected_results: invalid; error on :refs (key not in allowlist AND size)

test_cases.name: secret in refs.branch is rejected 422
expected_results: invalid; denylist match on a refs value; not persisted

technical_notes: Schema: Loopctl.Coordination.ChannelPost; context: Loopctl.Coordination; table: channel_posts (no existing collision — verified).

RLS: RlsHelpers.enable_rls(:channel_posts) — ENABLE (not FORCE) like other tables; runtime isolation is AdminRepo + explicit tenant_id filter, NOT RLS (see Knowledge/Projects). RLS is defense-in-depth.
project_id references(:projects, on_delete: :delete_all) — same FK/cascade as articles.project_id, but NOT NULL here (articles.project_id is nullable; a channel post always has a channel).
expires_at set in the context as now + @retention_days (30) — one authoritative constant in code, not a DB default.
Factor the knowledge secret-denylist regex into a shared helper and run it over body + refs values + key.

Unique key slot is the PARTIAL index channel_posts_session_key_uidx WHERE key IS NOT NULL. Decided under M7 as (tenant_id, project_id, session_id, key) — per-session, to avoid cross-session clobber — and HARDENED as shipped to (tenant_id, project_id, agent_id, session_id, key) by 20260718000000_harden_channel_posts_slot_and_ordering.exs, so the isolation does not rest on the spoofable client-supplied session_id. Because the index is PARTIAL, any ON CONFLICT against it must use a FRAGMENT conflict_target carrying the columns AND the WHERE predicate (US-39.2 AC-39.2.5) — a bare column list raises Postgres 42P10 at runtime.

Recency index as shipped is channel_posts_recent_seq_idx (tenant_id, project_id, inserted_at DESC, seq DESC); the original channel_posts_recent_idx (tenant_id, project_id, inserted_at DESC) was dropped as a redundant prefix by 20260718130000_drop_redundant_channel_posts_recent_idx.exs (US-40.A3).

acceptance_criteria_amendments.rationale: SPEC WAS WRONG, CODE IS RIGHT — reconciling the spec with shipped DDL; no code change. This story OWNS the schema, so leaving it stating the PRE-hardening tuple meant a future author re-deriving from it would rebuild the 4-column index and reintroduce the cross-agent clobber the hardening closed — and it contradicted its own dependent, US-39.2 AC-39.2.5. Two shipped migrations moved the DDL past this AC: 20260718000000_harden_channel_posts_slot_and_ordering.exs drops channel_posts_session_key_uidx and recreates it as (tenant_id, project_id, agent_id, session_id, key) WHERE key IS NOT NULL (the server-stamped agent_id joins the tuple so a spoofed session_id cannot reach another agent's slot) and adds seq (bigserial) + channel_posts_recent_seq_idx; 20260718130000_drop_redundant_channel_posts_recent_idx.exs drops channel_posts_recent_idx as a redundant prefix of the seq index (US-40.A3). The matching technical note ('Unique key slot is (tenant_id, project_id, session_id, key)...') was corrected in the SAME pass, and docs/repo-coordination-bus.md §3.5 — which had drifted further still, to a 3-column project-global slot — was corrected with it.
